options.A: Only when the patient complains of severe pain
options.B: Once every week during routine ward rounds
options.C: Immediately after the catheter is scheduled for removal
options.D: Regularly during every shift change and before medication administration

explanation: Frequent visual and manual checks catch early signs of infiltration, phlebitis, or dislodgement before they become severe. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which clinical finding in a patient who underwent a femoral EPS two hours ago requires immediate nursing intervention?

options.A: A normal heart rate of 72 beats per minute on telemetry
options.B: Expressed mild boredom regarding the period of restricted bedrest
options.C: A rapidly expanding, firm swelling at the groin puncture site
options.D: Mild bruising and skin tenderness directly around the bandage

explanation: An expanding groin swelling indicates active bleeding or hematoma formation, which can compromise circulation or lead to severe blood loss. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h5)

question: What is the primary distinction between palliative care and hospice care?

options.A: Palliative care is exclusively managed by physicians, while hospice care is delivered entirely by family members
options.B: Hospice care focuses strictly on symptom control without addressing psychological needs
options.C: Palliative care can be initiated at the time of diagnosis alongside curative treatment, whereas hospice care is for the final phase of life
options.D: Palliative care is only provided in specialized inpatient hospital units

explanation: Palliative care spans the entire trajectory of a serious illness and can run parallel to life-prolonging therapies, whereas hospice is specifically for end-of-life care. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T15#GNS324_U4_T15_h8)

question: Which bloodborne pathogen carries the highest risk of transmission following a single needle-stick injury?

options.A: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.B: Cytomegalovirus
options.C: Hepatitis C virus
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

question: What is the primary rationale for administering malaria chemoprophylaxis to pregnant women with sickle cell disease in endemic regions?

options.A: To prevent parasite-induced hemolysis that can precipitate a painful crisis
options.B: To enhance the oxygen-carrying capacity of maternal plasma

options.D: To eradicate chronic bacterial infections in the urinary tract

question: Why is a lumbar puncture commonly performed in patients suspected of having bacterial meningitis?

options.A: To visualize brain tissue via real-time imaging
options.B: To permanently lower systemic blood pressure
options.C: To deliver oral antibiotics directly to the stomach
options.D: To collect cerebrospinal fluid for analysis

question: How does the endocrine system typically respond to an excess of a specific target hormone?

options.A: The hypothalamus increases stimulant signals
options.B: Positive feedback loops stimulate higher gland output
options.C: Negative feedback loops decrease releasing hormone production
options.D: Target organs destroy the excess hormones locally

explanation: Homeostasis is maintained primarily through negative feedback, where high levels of a target hormone signal the brain to reduce upstream stimulation. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T14#GNS222_U2_T14_h1)

question: Which imaging sequence makes cerebrospinal fluid appear bright on a magnetic resonance scan?

options.A: Diffusion-weighted imaging

options.D: T2-weighted imaging

question: A patient presents to the emergency ward with an extremely painful, red, and swollen right big toe that woke them from sleep. What is the most likely initial nursing assessment priority?

options.B: Encourage immediate weight-bearing ambulation to assess functional ability

options.D: Apply hot moist compresses to the joint to promote local vasodilation
